searches.note: Twenty eight searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's. Nine were restricted to a primary body's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: cadelbosco.com twice (the wine's naming and change of 2008, the technical sheets), franciacorta.wine twice (the disciplinare of May 2024, the origins and regulations pages), bellavistawine.it twice (one returned no sheet, the other the house's own history), ninonegri.it three times (the 5 Stelle, the cellar and palace, Sfursat Carlo Negri), vinidivaltellina.it twice (the Sforzato and Valtellina Superiore rules), arpepe.com (the casks), consorziolugana.it (the decree, the zone, the Superiore) and cadeifrati.it (the friars and the family). The consortium search on origins served Ca' del Bosco's DOC of 1967 too and is counted under Bellavista; the search on the Valtellina Superiore DOCG's decree served the Sforzato DOCG of 2003 and is counted under Ar.Pe.Pe. Three searches found less than they sought and are counted: Bellavista's own domain gave no Satèn sheet, the namesake of Sfursat Carlo Negri, the year of the Gruppo Italiano Vini. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept in a record marked checked.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the bodies' own texts (the Franciacorta disciplinare of 2024 and the consortium's history, the ministry's Sforzato and Valtellina Superiore rules on the Valtellina consortium's site with the AIS copies, the Lugana consortium's rules and answers) and to the houses' own pages and technical sheets for their own dates and methods, then to the press, the importers and the merchants for the second source of each date, person and figure.

Where sources disagreed on a year or a figure (the lees of Annamaria Clementi, the oak and lees of the Satèn, the year Nino Negri joined the Gruppo Italiano Vini, the casks and bottle time of Rocce Rosse) the record gives what all allow; where a detail rested on one source or none (the hill named for its view, about six atmospheres, the namesake of Sfursat Carlo Negri, Castel Chiuro named for the palace, the naming of Rocce Rosse six years on, I Frati's late release) it was cut or replaced.

Sources whose title or address names a living person, or that are a writer's own site, were read in the results and never cited: a wine writer named in the Turbiana dispute and a Lombard sommeliers' magazine piece on Nino Negri whose address names its writer.

tested: The founding: the library's 1968 and the house's history page for the purchase of 1964 as the author read them; the consortium's regulations page for the DOC of 1967, a year before the house: confirmed as written.

The first vintage and the name: the house's site says the wine was first made in 1979, the year of the house's first vintage, as a Franciacorta Vintage, and the house's wine page that it took the name Cuvée Annamaria Clementi as a Riserva in 1989; a Falstaff supplement hosted by the house gives 1989 too: confirmed. One summary reads 1989 as the first vintage under the name, left open.

The change of 2008: the house's wine page says the name was shortened with the 2008 vintage and the wine became a Zero Dosage; the 2016 sheet prints no liqueur added, while the 2006 and 2007 sheets give about one gram of sugar and the 2003 sheet 7.5 millilitres of liqueur, all before the change. The author's doubt (an Extra Brut of about one gram) belongs to those older vintages: confirmed as written.

The making: the 2014 and 2016 sheets give free run juice fermented only in small oak casks of wood seasoned three years, six more months on the lees with the malolactic, disgorging without oxygen by a system the house designed and patented; the 2017 sheet describes the berry spa, a whirlpool wash of three soaking tanks: confirmed.

The years on the lees: an average of eight years on the 2016 sheet, eight years and five months on the 2007 sheet, over eight years in one merchant's listing: changed to about eight years in five places.

The grapes: the house's sheets give 55, 25 and 20 parts in a hundred of Chardonnay, Pinot Bianco and Pinot Nero for the 2007, 76, 9 and 15 for the 2014 and 83, 2 and 15 for the 2016; merchants give 55, 25 and 20 for the 2005 and 2006: changed.

The DOCG of 1995 and the Riserva's sixty months: the consortium's regulations page and the disciplinare of May 2024: confirmed. The R.S. 1980: at least forty years on its lees on the house's R.S. page, changed from forty two.

The rules: no living person in the fragment (the founder and the Champagne cellar master of 1979 met in the sources, never named); no price, score or volatile fact; service at 9 to 11 degrees Celsius sits within the Codex's 9 to 12 for an oak aged sparkling wine. The two questions each have one key, both confirmed (small oak casks for about six months; the founder's mother), with distractors of one kind.

open: Whether 1989 is the year the wine was renamed or its first vintage under the name: the house's page says it took the name in 1989, one press summary says from the 1989 vintage; the record follows the house.

The search summary of the house's wine page reads the name of 1989 as a tribute to the founder, the son's mother, a phrase that may count her as the founder; the library, the plan and the record call her the founder's mother, and the house tells its story as beginning with her purchase of 1964, so the integrator may wish to read the house's own wording.
The house's passage into the Santa Margherita group stays untold, as the author left it: no date was searched by the refuter.

tested: The founding and the hill: the house's Our utopia page, read through search, says it was founded in 1977 in Erbusco on the hill that bears its name, beginning with a few hectares, a family home and a winery beside it, and names the founder among the entrepreneurs of the area's revival in the 1970s: confirmed. It gives no reason for the hill's name, so the view goes; journeys to France were decisive by its account, so learned the craft goes.

The rules: the consortium's disciplinare of May 2024, read through search, gives 24 months on the lees for a Satèn, 30 for a Millesimato and 60 for a Riserva, at most five atmospheres for a Satèn, Brut only, and at least half Chardonnay: confirmed, save the 24 months, which is the minimum for a non vintage Satèn and not for this vintage wine.

The name Satèn: the consortium's origins and history timeline gives 1995 for the registration of the mark, the year of the DOCG, as the author's booklet does; one wine shop's article gives 1998 and is outweighed. Its origin is split (the French way of saying satin in one article, silk in several producers' words): changed to what all allow.

The DOC of 1967 and the DOCG of 1995: the consortium's regulations and origins pages: confirmed. The rules of 2008: the author's consortium booklet, with a search summary that every producer could make Satèn from 2008: kept as written.

The wine: the house's sheets for the 2018, 2020 and 2021 give Chardonnay alone, made only in the best years, 51, 45 and 42 parts in a hundred in small oak, and 45 months (2020) and an average of 48 months (2021) on the lees; older Gran Cuvée Satèn listings give 30 to 36 months: the oak share and the lees changed, the rest confirmed.
The pressure of the rest of the appellation: no figure in the rules; about six atmospheres goes from the story, the card and the question.

The rules of the house: no living person in the fragment (the founder, his daughter in the cellar and the house's mentor met, the mentor already in people.json); no price or score. The two questions each have one key (the lower pressure; the hill's name), both confirmed, the explanations teaching why the nearest wrong option is wrong.

changed.was: About half the base wine ferments and matures in small oak barrels and the rest in stainless steel, the share moving with the year. The blend is bottled with less sugar for the second fermentation, so the pressure stays low, and it rests for years on its lees, far beyond the 24 months the rules ask, before a Brut dosage.
changed.now: Some two fifths to half of the base wine ferments and matures in small oak barrels and the rest in stainless steel, the share moving with the year. The blend is bottled with less sugar for the second fermentation, so the pressure stays low, and it rests some four years on its lees by the house's own sheets, beyond the thirty months the rules ask of a vintage Franciacorta, before a Brut dosage.
changed.why: The rules ask 24 months on the lees of a Satèn but 30 of a Millesimato, and Bellavista's Satèn is a vintage wine, so the 24 months was the wrong minimum. The house's sheets give 45 months for the 2020 and an average of 48 for the 2021, so for years becomes some four years by the house's own sheets; the share in small oak is 42 parts in a hundred for the 2021, 45 for the 2020 and 51 for the 2018, so about half becomes two fifths to half.

tested: The founder and 1897: the house's cellar page says that after his marriage the founder, from Aprica, decided to move to Chiuro and set up a wine producing business, and Vinicum agrees; the company was entered with the Sondrio chamber of commerce in 1925: confirmed, with the marriage no longer placed in Chiuro and the business no longer a trade. The founder stays unnamed, the house and Vinicum naming him Nino where a Dutch merchant says Carlo.

The palace: the house's page says the Duke of Milan gave the fifteenth century palace to a soldier and captain of the Quadrio family, making him Governor of the Valtellina, who dug the four floors of cellars and sold wine: changed to the gift with the governorship.

1956 for the first Sfursat: Vinicum and Callmewine, beside the author's Decanter and Il Sole 24 Ore: confirmed. 1983 for the first 5 Stelle: Vinicum and Wine Spectator, which gives that wine twenty months in new French oak: confirmed, the hedge kept.

The Gruppo Italiano Vini: Decanter and a merchant give 1986, a guide of 1990 hosted by Ca' del Bosco lists Negri in the group, and the house's own cellar page says the group acquired it at the end of the 1970s: changed to by 1986, and the story question no longer rests on the year.

The rules: the ministry's disciplinare on the consortium's site gives pressing from 1 December unless the region allows it sooner when the weather calls for it, at least 14 degrees after drying, at least nine parts in ten Nebbiolo; the consortium gives twenty months of ageing, twelve in wood, and the DOCG of 2003, which the AIS copy of the rules dates by the decree of 19 March 2003; the house's page says the 2018 was pressed on 15 November after a warm drying: changed.

The sites: the house's page gives the Valtellina DOC and DOCG zones on the Rhaetian Alps, south facing at 300 to 550 metres, on loose, shallow sandy silt: confirmed. The drying: about three months in most accounts, many months in Decanter: some months stands.

The barriques: sixteen months in new Allier and Nevers barriques for the 2001 (Decanter) and the 2021 (Callmewine), eighteen for the 2009 (Tastingbook), twenty in Eataly's account and for the 1983 (Wine Spectator): confirmed as sixteen to twenty months.

The others: the house's pages for Sfursat Carlo Negri (natural drying in the dry alpine air), Quadrio (named for the palace) and Vigna Fracia (Valgella, part of the house since 1897): changed. No living person in the fragment; the questions each have one key.

tested: The family and the house: Skurnik, an Italian trade account and a wine reference agree that the Pelizzatti brand was sold to a Swiss food and wine multinational in 1973 after family troubles, that the vineyards were leased on a ten year contract, and that in 1984 the refounder took them back and began under Ar.Pe.Pe., an acronym of his name; 1860 for the family's wine in listings and, as the author read it, on the house's own page: confirmed. The sources agree that the refounder died in 2004, so he is not living; no birth year was found, so he stays described.

Rocce Rosse: Skurnik, K&L and the house's press page on the fortieth year vertical give 1984 for the first Sassella Riserva and the iron rich red rock of the subzone for its name; that the name came six years later rests on one account: changed.

The making: the house's pages and the press they host give macerations of about 35 days (2002, in steel), 69 (in wooden vats), 97 (2016, in wooden vats) and about 130, large casks of chestnut and oak (acacia in one account) for 34 to 48 months, cement only in some vintages, and at least one or at least three years in bottle by account: changed to say what all allow.

The appellation: the AIS copy of the disciplinare gives the DOC of 11 August 1968 and the DOCG of 24 June 1998; the consortium gives five subzones, Maroggia, Sassella, Grumello, Inferno and Valgella, and 36 months for a Riserva: confirmed as written.
The grape and the sites: entirely Chiavennasca in two merchants' accounts; the vines at about 400 to 500 metres facing south or south east, not given a height in the record: confirmed as written.

The rules: no living person in the fragment; no price, score or award (the guide's prize for the 2007 and the 2016, met in the sources, is not told). The two questions each have one key (a long maceration then years in large casks; 1973), confirmed.

changed.was: The wine then ages some three to four years in large casks, chestnut among them, and rests in cement and for at least three years in bottle before release.
changed.now: The wine then ages some three to four years in large casks of chestnut and oak, in some years with a spell in cement, and rests for years in bottle before release.
changed.why: The house's pages and the press it hosts give large casks of chestnut and oak, acacia in one account, for 34 to 48 months by vintage, and cement only in some vintages (the 2005, the 2016); the bottle time is at least three years in one account and at least a year in another, so the record says for years.

tested: The friars: the house's own pages, read through search on its domain, say that from 1450 a detachment of Discalced Carmelites from the monastery at Desenzano settled there and made wine, and that a document of 1782 names the house with its cellar as the place of the friars: confirmed as the house's account.

The family: the house's pages, the Valpolicella consortium's producer page and Vinorandum give 1939 for the grower's move from Montecchia di Crosara into the house at Lugana di Sirmione, the son's signing of the first disciplinare of 1967 and the first bottle of Lugana DOC in 1969: confirmed. The son died in 2012; the widow and the children who run the estate are living and are not named.

The appellation: the Lugana consortium gives the decree of 21 July 1967, a zone of all of Sirmione and parts of Desenzano, Lonato, Pozzolengo and Peschiera del Garda delimited in 1967 and never changed, the Superiore from 1998 aged at least a year, and the Riserva at 24 months: confirmed as written.

The grape: the rules name the Trebbiano di Soave vine known locally as Turbiana or Trebbiano di Lugana; a Vitis study found Verdicchio and Trebbiano di Soave almost identical and Trebbiano di Lugana very close; the consortium holds Turbiana distinct: changed to close to both.
The wine: Turbiana alone on calcareous moraine (Superiore.de), steel at controlled temperature and some six months on fine lees (two Italian merchants): confirmed as written.

The others: Brolettino ten months in barriques (Callmewine, Superiore.de); the late release Privilegio di Famiglia, seven to eight months in barrique and five years in bottle, named Brolettino by Xtrawine and Delicando and I Frati by one German merchant: changed. No living person in the fragment; the questions each have one key (Turbiana; 1967), confirmed.

The widow of Pietro Dal Cero and the refounder's widow at Ar.Pe.Pe. are met by their given names only and are not listed. The author's list of living names (the cellar masters and winemakers of Bellavista and Nino Negri, the refounder's three children at Ar.Pe.Pe., a Ca' del Bosco planter) stands beside this one and was not re-met. swapNote: The author proposed no swap, and the refuter proposes none. The plan's note on Bellavista asked the author to propose Alma if the house or two sources set it at the head of the range; no source of the refuter's does, the house's sheets show the Satèn as its vintage Chardonnay made only in the best years, and the prestige Riserva carries the living founder's name, so the Satèn stays the flagship taught.
planNotes: ca-del-bosco: the note is answered: the house prints Annamaria Clementi with the designation Franciacorta Riserva, and the founder's mother stays described for want of a birth year in two sources.
bellavista: the note is answered: the label is Franciacorta Satèn with the vintage, Chardonnay alone on the house's sheets for the 2018, 2020 and 2021; no swap to Alma.

nino-negri: the why's long the valley's largest rests on no source read by the author or the refuter; the read-together agent may wish to drop it. The note is answered: the house heads the wine Sfursat 5 Stelle, Sforzato di Valtellina DOCG.

arpepe: the note is answered: Rocce Rosse is still made as a Valtellina Superiore Sassella Riserva in the years the family judges exceptional and is held for years in cask and bottle; the refounder died in 2004 by the sources read, so the note's living member of the family applies to his children.
ca-dei-frati: the note is answered: 1939 stands on the house's pages, the Valpolicella consortium's producer page and Vinorandum; the label is Lugana I Frati, Turbiana alone.
